escalations.question: The 10 bare `font-weight: 600` declarations across 5 renderer directories have no token. Does the theme contract gain a semibold weight, or do the 10 sites move onto the existing 500/700 tokens?
escalations.answer: Add the semibold token. The contract gains `--oc-weight-semibold` at 600 as an additions-only amendment, and all 10 sites move onto it. The user took the first option as recommended.

options.summary: Add `--oc-weight-semibold` (600) to TOKENS and tokens.css, additions-only, and move all 10 declarations onto it.
options.rationale: All 10 sites are one role - headings and emphatic labels - and five directories independently reached for the same bare value for the same reason. That is the exact shape the sub-session 3 amendment recorded when it added seven tokens including `--oc-weight-bold`. Additions-only means no existing component's appearance changes.

options.summary: Move the 10 declarations onto the existing `--oc-weight-medium` (500) or `--oc-weight-bold` (700).
options.rationale: No contract change at all. But it is a visible typography change at 10 sites in 5 directories, and it requires a per-site visual judgment about which way each one goes - which is precisely the decision T10 declined to make when it pinned the value instead.

options.summary: Accept the bare 600s and leave `PRE_TOKEN_SHELL_DECLARATIONS` pinning them.
options.rationale: Costs nothing now. Leaves the theme contract's rule 3 - no component hardcodes a value, every one comes from `var(--oc-*)` - violated at 10 sites, and leaves a two-sided pin holding a known defect in place.

escalations.question: Four full-window scrims are opaque (`background: var(--oc-bg-app)`) because the token set has no alpha layer, so a dialog hides the window rather than veiling it. Does the contract gain an overlay token, and does the fix cover all four sites or only the one the backlog filed?
escalations.answer: One token, all four scrims. Add a single overlay token to the theme contract and convert Helm, DeletePodDialog, NewPodDialog and BeachcomberPreviewDialog together. The user took the first option as recommended.

options.summary: Add one overlay token and convert all four scrims together.
options.rationale: A census of all 11 `--oc-bg-app` consumers in CSS found exactly four full-window scrims, all with the identical declaration triple, and one of them records the missing alpha layer as the cause for itself and for a sibling. One cause, one token, one consistent result across every dialog in the app.

options.summary: Add the token but convert only `.confirmScrim`, the single site the backlog filed.
options.rationale: Matches the literal filed scope and the handoff brief's 'sole consumer' note. It would leave three dialogs opaque while a fourth veils - a visible inconsistency nobody asked for, and a near-certain re-file.

options.summary: Accept all four as opaque and correct the backlog's measurement instead.
options.rationale: Changes no CSS, but replaces the 'sole consumer' note with the four-site census so a later session scopes it correctly. Defers a real visual defect while closing the measurement error that hid its breadth.

escalations.question: `PanelBar`'s per-panel button carries `aria-pressed`, which truthfully reports open state but sits on a button that can never un-press itself, because the frozen contract requires a re-click on the open panel's own button to be a no-op. Keep `aria-pressed`, move to `aria-current`, or make the strip a tablist with `aria-selected`?
escalations.answer: Move to `aria-current="true"`. This sanctions the edit to PanelBar.test.tsx:50-59 that C1's criterion 11 protected. The user took the first option as recommended.

options.summary: Replace `aria-pressed={open === key}` with `aria-current` on the open panel's button.
options.rationale: MDN defines aria-current as indicating that the element 'represents the current item within a container or set of related elements', with the value `true` meaning the current item in a set. One button in a strip of panel buttons is exactly that. The panel strip is not a toggle, so the toggle attribute is the wrong one.

options.summary: Give the strip `role="tablist"` with `role="tab"` buttons and `aria-selected`.
options.rationale: The strictest reading of the spec: MDN warns that when something is selected rather than current, such as a tab in a tablist, aria-selected is the attribute, and explicitly says not to substitute aria-current for aria-selected on a tab. But it pulls in roles, APG arrow-key navigation and tabpanel wiring, and it interacts with the frozen no-dialog-on-re-click rule.

options.summary: Keep `aria-pressed` and record in the docblock why it stays.
options.rationale: Cheapest, and touches no protected test. But the external evidence cuts against it: aria-pressed is defined for toggle buttons with two reachable states and this button has one. Nothing is announced incorrectly - the attribute remains a truthful state indicator - it is the control's affordance that is misdescribed.

escalations.question: `resetHelmForReopen` nulls `incoming` through a whole-state reset, so the live contract's clearing list - declared EXHAUSTIVE over four named events - is not exhaustive as written. The behaviour is correct; only the prose is wrong. Amend the live contract, rescope the word, or record it and amend nothing?
escalations.answer: Name the whole-state reset in the live contract, stamped with this session's slug per the file's existing amendment convention, and complete `resetHelmForReopen`'s own docblock. No code change. The user took the first option as recommended.

options.summary: Amend the live clearing list to name the panel-close whole-state reset, and complete the store method's docblock.
options.rationale: The live contract already uses an `ADDED by session <slug>` convention, so the amendment has a stamped home that does not touch any frozen session artifact. The store method's own docblock names the document and the draft but not `incoming`, so it has the same hole. After the edit, an auditor's question is answerable from the contract alone.

options.summary: Narrow the claim instead: the list is exhaustive over events that clear `incoming` alone, and a whole-state reset is a separate class.
options.rationale: Arguably truer to what the original author meant, and a smaller edit. It leaves a reader to infer that the whole-state reset class exists rather than seeing it named, which is most of the value of fixing it at all.

options.summary: Leave both the contract and the docblock; file it in the backlog's Informational section.
options.rationale: That section already parks falsified claims in frozen contracts that can never be edited. But this claim sits in a live contract under `src/`, not in a frozen artifact, so unlike those it can actually be fixed - which makes parking it a weaker fit than it first looks.

escalations.question: T3's acceptance criteria 4 and 8 are arithmetically incompatible as frozen. Criterion 4 MANDATES that the overlay token derive its hue from `--oc-bg-app` via `color-mix` and introduce no colour literal; that necessarily adds an eighth `var(--oc-bg-app)` occurrence at the token's own definition site in `styles/tokens.css`, inside criterion 8's `--include="*.css"` glob. Criterion 8 demands the count be exactly 7. Reaching 7 would require a hex literal, violating criterion 4. Amend the frozen criterion, or record criterion 8 as not met on its letter?
escalations.answer: Amend criterion 8 to scope its count to consumers, excluding the token definition site, keeping the total at 7. The user took the first option as recommended. Performed as amendment A1.

options.summary: Scope criterion 8's command to exclude the token definition site, keeping the expected total at 7.
options.rationale: The criterion's own subject has always been the seven CONSUMERS it names by file and line - its text reads 'the SEVEN other `--oc-bg-app` consumers' and asserts 'the seven matching file:line pairs are exactly those listed'. The definition of a different token is not a consumer of this one. The filter expresses what the criterion meant rather than relaxing what it checks, and both the count and the exactly-those-listed claim stay true.

options.summary: Change the expected total from 7 to 8 and name the definition site as the expected eighth occurrence.
options.rationale: The smallest possible edit to the frozen text. But it leaves a criterion whose count says 8 while its prose names seven files and asserts the matches are exactly those listed, so a later reader must reconstruct why the two numbers disagree - the stale-prose trap this session exists to close.

options.summary: Leave the frozen criterion untouched and record criterion 8 as not met on its letter.
options.rationale: Preserves the frozen artifact perfectly and costs no amendment record. But it writes a false negative into the Gate 3 per-criterion table against work that is correct, and a later reader of `coverage.md` sees a failed criterion where none failed.

amendments.before: T3 criterion 8's evidence required `grep -rno "var(--oc-bg-app)" src/renderer --include="*.css" | wc -l` to print exactly 7 after the change, unfiltered.
amendments.after: The same grep piped through `grep -v "^src/renderer/src/styles/tokens.css:"` must print exactly 7, with the unfiltered form recorded as printing 8; the amendment states why criteria 4 and 8 could not both hold as frozen.
